summary: Jackson County, OR summit cupola lookout built 1917, replaced 1931, abandoned 1936 and destroyed or removed in 1955; a foundation is reported at the summit.

facts.design: Cupola house twelve feet square with a six-foot-square cupola (1917); replacement house of 1931 set on a cement and stone foundation
facts.status_note: Second house destroyed or removed in 1955; sources describe a remaining foundation at the summit

staffing.status: Ernest W. Smith first lookout from September 1917; J.F.G. Cone from 1922 for about eight years; James Radcliffe named in 1933; post empty in 1935; abandoned in 1936

access.note: Summit lies in the Sky Lakes Wilderness and is reached by a hiking trail; no closure is mentioned in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Five-mile Mt. McLoughlin Trail #3716 from the trailhead, with an elevation gain of about 4,000 feet; the Forest Service notes there is no water on the summit trail

events.note: Cupola house erected on the summit; finished at the start of October 1917 (Willhite); the register and firelookout.com date the cabin to 1917
Ernest W. Smith, the first lookout, from September 1917; he signaled by light to stations up to 20 miles away
J.F.G. Cone lookout for about eight years (Willhite); Forest Lookouts describes him as a sociable hermit
Storms and ice in 1930 weakened the house; a slightly larger replacement on a cement and stone foundation was completed in 1931
James Radcliffe of Medford appointed lookout, taking up duties about July 1
Post unoccupied for the first fire season in several years; no reason given
Officially abandoned in favor of lower points such as Robinson Butte
Destroyed after vandalism and misuse; a crew pushed it over the side of the peak. The register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Photo caption: foundation of the second lookout (photo by Tom Lopez)
Photo caption: foundation of the second lookout
Registered March 26, 2011 as US 883, OR 250; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 1931 replacement cupola lookout was used for about one season. The Forest Lookouts history names a lookout in 1933 and records the post as empty in 1935, which points to more than one season. The story follows the history.
The register says it was removed in 1955; firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts history say it was destroyed, with vandalism and misuse named as the cause.

resolved_conflicts.field: cause of the first cabin's replacement
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts history gives storms and ice in 1930 as the reason the house was replaced. The Oregon Hikers guide says fierce winds destroyed the first wooden cabin. The sources do not reconcile the two accounts.

A 1933 Forest Lookouts item says the lookout was first occupied in 1918. The Medford Sun item of 19 September 1917 and the Willhite history place Ernest W. Smith on the summit from September 1917. The story follows the 1917 items.

notes_for_editor: Brief had access unknown; the sources describe a hiking route to the summit in the Sky Lakes Wilderness, so access is recorded as public. The remaining foundation rests on one undated hiking guide and on 1973 and 1987 photo captions; no source describes the summit today in more detail. The 1930 storms and the wind account conflict and are both reported.
